prompt: A function $f$ is increasing and concave down on $[a, b]$. Which of the following approximations of $\int_a^b f(x) \, dx$ is guaranteed to be an OVERESTIMATE?

choices.label: None of these can be an overestimate.

hint: Two separate facts decide this: increasing vs. decreasing controls left/right sums; concave up vs. down controls trapezoids and midpoints.

hints.text: Two separate facts decide this: increasing vs. decreasing controls left/right sums; concave up vs. down controls trapezoids and midpoints.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Sketch $y = \sqrt{x}$ on $[0, 4]$ — increasing and concave down. Draw one right-endpoint rectangle: its top edge sits above the curve. Draw one trapezoid: its slanted top cuts below the arching curve.
Increasing: each right-endpoint rectangle is taller than the curve, so the right sum overestimates; the left sum underestimates. Concave down: chords lie below the curve, so trapezoids underestimate.
Only the right Riemann sum is guaranteed too big: choice A.

explanation: For an INCREASING function, the right endpoint is the highest point on each subinterval, so right rectangles poke above the curve: the right sum is an overestimate. Left rectangles sit below: an underestimate.
For a CONCAVE DOWN function, the chord joining two points on the graph lies below the graph, so each trapezoid misses some area: the trapezoidal sum is an underestimate.
The only guaranteed overestimate listed is the right Riemann sum, choice A. (A midpoint sum would also overestimate for concave down, but it is not offered.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with real numbers
steps: Take $f(x) = \sqrt{x}$ on $[0, 4]$, exact integral $\frac{16}{3} \approx 5.33$, with $4$ subintervals.
Right sum: $1(1 + 1.414 + 1.732 + 2) \approx 6.15$ (over). Left sum: $1(0 + 1 + 1.414 + 1.732) \approx 4.15$ (under). Trapezoid: average of those, $\approx 5.15$ (under).
The numbers match the reasoning: only the right sum is too big.
